tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description uses imperative-style framing ('Use this skill when...'), focuses on user-facing symptoms (slow/throttled endpoints, silent async failures, scaling questions) rather than implementation details, explicitly lists numerous trigger contexts including cases where the user doesn't name the domain directly (e.g., 'even if they do not mention cold start, provisioned concurrency...'), and while lengthy, it is a single cohesive paragraph appropriate for the breadth of triggers it must cover.
tests.evidence: Use this skill when a serverless endpoint is slow or throttled after idle periods... even if they do not mention cold start, provisioned concurrency, SNS topics, InputLocation, backlog scaling or AsyncInferenceConfig by name.

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body jumps straight to domain-specific procedures (check-ids, router table, known-causes) without explaining generic concepts like what SageMaker or CloudWatch are. It assumes the agent already knows AWS basics and focuses on project-specific conventions.
tests.evidence: Grounded in the LLM-SM check family under checks-sagemaker-serverless-async.md — the LLM-SM-SERVE-* sub-family for serverless & async inference; load it before assigning any check-id or severity.

tests.name: Detailed reference materials must not be in body
tests.reasoning: The body keeps a short index table of check-ids with one-line descriptions and routes detailed detection rules, remediations, and citations to references/ files rather than embedding them inline.
tests.evidence: The full six-column detection rules, remediations, and citations live in the reference — the table below is a what-it-catches index.

tests.name: Reference files must be linked
tests.reasoning: Every file in references/ (checks-sagemaker-serverless-async.md, collection-reference.md, api-quirks.md, metrics-and-logs.md, cloudwatch-alarm-reference.md, known-causes.md) is linked with markdown link syntax in the body.

tests.name: Reference links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: Each reference link is paired with a clear trigger condition for when to load it, e.g. tied to symptoms in the Router table or specific checks.
tests.evidence: Load [checks-sagemaker-serverless-async.md](references/checks-sagemaker-serverless-async.md) before writing any finding: it holds the full detection rules, remediations, and citations.

tests.name: Reference path format
tests.reasoning: All reference links use relative paths rooted at references/ with no absolute paths or traversals.

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: Fragile operations (guardrails, validation checklist, break-fix) are given exact prescriptive steps, while flexible areas like which signal to inspect first explain purpose via the router rather than rigid scripts.
tests.evidence: Non-negotiable, at every step: 1. Read-only. Never call CreateEndpoint...

tests.name: Defaults, not menus
tests.reasoning: The router table designates a clear 'first read' default API call per symptom, with a secondary reference as escape hatch rather than listing all options equally.

tests.name: Favor procedures over declarations
tests.reasoning: The skill teaches a generalizable diagnostic approach (match symptom → check catalog → confirm via collection calls → report) rather than a one-off instance-specific task.
tests.evidence: Match the symptom, confirm with the collection calls, then report with the check-id and severity from the catalog.

tests.name: Gotchas section
tests.reasoning: The skill has an explicit 'Common wrong answers' section plus an 'Error Handling' section documenting non-obvious traps like misreading CloudWatch no-datapoints or InService with zero instances.
tests.evidence: "No `ModelSetupTime` datapoints came back, so there is no cold start and the backlog is empty." Absent CloudWatch datapoints mean no traffic or nothing emitted in the window, not a measured zero.
